Proof 1: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #1):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

ID: a0f702412051 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n)

Mutation test: Removing 'continuous on [a,b]': f(x)=|x| on [-1,1] with division at 0 fails

Provenance: Variation #1 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 2: Heine-Borel: closed bounded subset of R^n is compact

Statement: Heine-Borel: closed bounded subset of R^n is compact

Hypotheses: K subset R^n, K closed, K bounded

Conclusion: K is compact

Definitions: closed, bounded, compact, Heine-Borel

Proof (Variation #2):

Step 1: K bounded => K subset [-M,M]^n (closed cube)

Step 2: Cover K by open sets in R^n

Step 3: Extend cover to cover the cube

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Step 5: Closed subset of compact space is compact

ID: ef6cdc560c1d | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^2)

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': R^n itself is closed but not compact

Provenance: Variation #2 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 3: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #3):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

ID: feb89b1a3f82 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n log n)

Mutation test: Removing 'dominated': f_n = n*1_{[0,1/n]}, integral = 1 for all n, f=0

Provenance: Variation #3 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 4: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #4):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

ID: 53d1e2148e4b | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(1)

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': x_n = n has no convergent subsequence

Provenance: Variation #4 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 81: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #81):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #131):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Mutation test: Removing 'dominated': f_n = n*1_{[0,1/n]}, integral = 1 for all n, f=0

Proof 132: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #132):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': x_n = n has no convergent subsequence

Proof 133: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #133):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Step 1: K bounded => K subset [-M,M]^n (closed cube)

Step 2: Cover K by open sets in R^n

Step 3: Extend cover to cover the cube

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Step 5: Closed subset of compact space is compact

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #157):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Proof 159: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #159):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 160: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #160):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #183):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

ID: e8979d4b8939 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n log n)

Mutation test: Removing 'dominated': f_n = n*1_{[0,1/n]}, integral = 1 for all n, f=0

Provenance: Variation #183 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 184: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #184):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

ID: e4bce90690a5 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(1)

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': x_n = n has no convergent subsequence

Provenance: Variation #184 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 185: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #185):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

ID: a411658f50f1 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^3)

Mutation test: Removing 'continuous on [a,b]': f(x)=|x| on [-1,1] with division at 0 fails

Provenance: Variation #185 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Statement: Heine-Borel: closed bounded subset of R^n is compact

Proof (Variation #186):

Step 1: K bounded => K subset [-M,M]^n (closed cube)

Step 2: Cover K by open sets in R^n

Step 3: Extend cover to cover the cube

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Step 5: Closed subset of compact space is compact

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #209):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Proof 211: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #211):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 212: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #212):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #235):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

ID: 653c9384c0ee | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^3)

Mutation test: Removing 'dominated': f_n = n*1_{[0,1/n]}, integral = 1 for all n, f=0

Provenance: Variation #235 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 236: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #236):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

ID: 90a8987494e8 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n)

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': x_n = n has no convergent subsequence

Provenance: Variation #236 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 237: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #237):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

ID: ba361ec872b4 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^2)

Mutation test: Removing 'continuous on [a,b]': f(x)=|x| on [-1,1] with division at 0 fails

Statement: Heine-Borel: closed bounded subset of R^n is compact

Hypotheses: K subset R^n, K closed, K bounded

Proof (Variation #238):

Step 1: K bounded => K subset [-M,M]^n (closed cube)

Step 2: Cover K by open sets in R^n

Step 3: Extend cover to cover the cube

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Step 5: Closed subset of compact space is compact

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #261):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Mutation test: Removing 'continuous on [a,b]': f(x)=|x| on [-1,1] with division at 0 fails

Statement: Heine-Borel: closed bounded subset of R^n is compact

Hypotheses: K subset R^n, K closed, K bounded

Conclusion: K is compact

Definitions: closed, bounded, compact, Heine-Borel

Proof (Variation #262):

Step 1: K bounded => K subset [-M,M]^n (closed cube)

Step 2: Cover K by open sets in R^n

Step 3: Extend cover to cover the cube

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Step 5: Closed subset of compact space is compact

Proof 263: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #263):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

ID: 97d5e38596ed | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n log n)

Mutation test: Removing 'dominated': f_n = n*1_{[0,1/n]}, integral = 1 for all n, f=0

Provenance: Variation #263 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 264: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #264):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': x_n = n has no convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #287):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

ID: bd950ec8fd0d | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^2)

Mutation test: Removing 'dominated': f_n = n*1_{[0,1/n]}, integral = 1 for all n, f=0

Provenance: Variation #287 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 288: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #288):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': x_n = n has no convergent subsequence

Proof 289: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #289):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Mutation test: Removing 'continuous on [a,b]': f(x)=|x| on [-1,1] with division at 0 fails

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #313):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Proof 315: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #315):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 316: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #316):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #339):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 340: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #340):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Proof 341: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #341):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #365):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Proof (Variation #366):

Step 2: Cover K by open sets in R^n

Step 3: Extend cover to cover the cube

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Step 5: Closed subset of compact space is compact

Proof 367: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #367):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 368: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #368):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #391):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

ID: c8825da4fcf9 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n)

Mutation test: Removing 'dominated': f_n = n*1_{[0,1/n]}, integral = 1 for all n, f=0

Proof 392: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #392):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': x_n = n has no convergent subsequence

Proof 393: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #393):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Mutation test: Removing 'continuous on [a,b]': f(x)=|x| on [-1,1] with division at 0 fails

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #417):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Proof 419: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #419):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 420: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #420):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #443):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Mutation test: Removing 'dominated': f_n = n*1_{[0,1/n]}, integral = 1 for all n, f=0

Proof 444: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #444):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': x_n = n has no convergent subsequence

Proof 445: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #445):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Mutation test: Removing 'continuous on [a,b]': f(x)=|x| on [-1,1] with division at 0 fails

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #469):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Proof 471: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #471):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #495):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 496: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #496):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Proof 497: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #497):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #521):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Proof (Variation #522):

Step 3: Extend cover to cover the cube

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Step 5: Closed subset of compact space is compact

Proof 523: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #523):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 524: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #524):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #547):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 548: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #548):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Proof 549: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #549):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #573):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: Heine-Borel: closed bounded subset of R^n is compact

Hypotheses: K subset R^n, K closed, K bounded

Conclusion: K is compact

Definitions: closed, bounded, compact, Heine-Borel

Proof (Variation #574):

Step 1: K bounded => K subset [-M,M]^n (closed cube)

Step 2: Cover K by open sets in R^n

Step 3: Extend cover to cover the cube

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Step 5: Closed subset of compact space is compact

Proof 575: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #575):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 576: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #576):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #599):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Mutation test: Removing 'dominated': f_n = n*1_{[0,1/n]}, integral = 1 for all n, f=0

Provenance: Variation #599 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 600: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #600):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

ID: 32a798b119c5 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^3)

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': x_n = n has no convergent subsequence

Provenance: Variation #600 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 601: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #601):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Step 2: Cover K by open sets in R^n

Step 3: Extend cover to cover the cube

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Step 5: Closed subset of compact space is compact

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #625):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

ID: ff0fdfc2cbef | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^3)

Mutation test: Removing 'continuous on [a,b]': f(x)=|x| on [-1,1] with division at 0 fails

Proof 626: Heine-Borel: closed bounded subset of R^n is compact

Statement: Heine-Borel: closed bounded subset of R^n is compact

Hypotheses: K subset R^n, K closed, K bounded

Conclusion: K is compact

Definitions: closed, bounded, compact, Heine-Borel

Proof (Variation #626):

Step 1: K bounded => K subset [-M,M]^n (closed cube)

Step 2: Cover K by open sets in R^n

Step 3: Extend cover to cover the cube

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Step 5: Closed subset of compact space is compact

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': R^n itself is closed but not compact

Proof 627: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #627):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

ID: e760c2cb031b | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^2)

Mutation test: Removing 'dominated': f_n = n*1_{[0,1/n]}, integral = 1 for all n, f=0

Provenance: Variation #627 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 628: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #628):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': x_n = n has no convergent subsequence

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #651):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Mutation test: Removing 'dominated': f_n = n*1_{[0,1/n]}, integral = 1 for all n, f=0

Provenance: Variation #651 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 652: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Statement: Bolzano-Weierstrass: bounded sequence in R has convergent subsequence

Hypotheses: sequence (x_n) bounded in R

Conclusion: convergent subsequence exists

Definitions: bounded, convergent, subsequence, nested intervals

Proof (Variation #652):

Step 1: Sequence lies in some [a,b]

Step 2: Bisect [a,b], one half contains infinitely many terms

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

ID: 1ade8068b1a5 | Status: UNFORMALIZED | Complexity: O(n^2)

Mutation test: Removing 'bounded': x_n = n has no convergent subsequence

Provenance: Variation #652 for theorem in domain Math_Analysis

Proof 653: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #653):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Step 3: Extend cover to cover the cube

Step 4: Cube is compact (standard result for products of intervals)

Step 5: Closed subset of compact space is compact

Proof 677: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #677):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Proof 679: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #679):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 705: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #705):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 757: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #757):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #783):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 807: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #807):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 809: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #809):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Proof 833: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Statement: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Hypotheses: f continuous on [a,b], f differentiable on (a,b)

Conclusion: exists c in (a,b) with f'(c) = avg slope

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #833):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Proof 835: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #835):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Step 3: Choose that half as [a_1,b_1]

Step 4: Repeat: find nested intervals [a_n,b_n] with diam -> 0

Step 5: Each contains infinitely many terms

Step 6: Pick x_{n_k} from k-th interval

Step 7: (x_{n_k}) is Cauchy hence convergent

Proof 859: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Proof (Variation #859):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof 861: MVT: f continuous on [a,b], diff on (a,b) => f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Definitions: continuous, differentiable, mean value

Proof (Variation #861):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 2: g(a) = g(b) = 0

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 5: g'(c) = f'(c) - (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a) = 0

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof (Variation #913):

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)

Proof (Variation #965):

Step 1: Define g(x) = f(x) - f(a) - [(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)]*(x-a)

Step 3: g is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b)

Step 4: By Rolle's theorem, g'(c) = 0 for some c in (a,b)

Step 6: Therefore f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a)

Proof 991: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Statement: DCT: f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g integrable => integral f_n -> integral f

Hypotheses: f_n measurable, f_n -> f a.e., |f_n| <= g, g integrable

Conclusion: integral f_n converges to integral f

Definitions: dominated convergence, integral, Measurability

Proof (Variation #991):

Step 1: Apply Fatou's lemma to g + f_n >= 0

Step 2: liminf integral(g + f_n) >= integral(g + f)

Step 3: integral(g) + liminf integral(f_n) >= integral(g) + integral(f)

Step 4: Apply Fatou's lemma to g - f_n >= 0

Step 5: liminf integral(g - f_n) >= integral(g - f)

Step 6: integral(g) + liminf integral(-f_n) >= integral(g) - integral(f)

Step 7: Combine: lim integral(f_n) = integral(f)
